data.title: Open Graph
data.tagline: og:* metadata that describes a shared-link preview
data.learningOutcome: You can map a share card's title, description, image, and URL to Open Graph fields and verify them in an external preview rather than only a page screenshot.
data.description: When an article link is sent through a chat or social platform, the platform can read og:title, og:description, og:image, and og:url to build a preview card. A page image working in the browser does not prove that the external platform received the share image, and platforms may cache an old result.

learning.assumes: You have seen a link preview in a chat or found that a shared link showed only a bare URL.
learning.outcome: You can map a share card's title, description, image, and URL to Open Graph fields and verify them in an external preview rather than only a page screenshot.

distinctions.label: Page metadata
distinctions.explanation: Open Graph is the share-focused group within Page Metadata; page metadata also covers tabs, search, and installation consumers.

distinctions.label: Image
distinctions.explanation: Open Graph says which image a share card should use; Image owns the image's page display, ratio, and loading result.

explanation.title: Four basic outputs should map cleanly
explanation.text: og:title, og:description, og:image, and og:url provide the title, description, image, and address. The image must be readable from a public URL by the sharing platform, not only on a local machine or behind a login.

explanation.title: The platform may keep an old fetch
explanation.text: After changing fields, request or refresh the platform preview and inspect the real card. Correct page source proves the fields were emitted, not that a cached preview has updated.

data.boundary: Open Graph focuses on external link previews; SEO is the broader search-presentation topic; an Image is the image shown in a page or asset. A working Hero image does not prove that og:image is correct.

lessonPractice.title: The article Hero image works on the page, but the shared card has no image. What should be fixed?

options.label: Add or fix og:image with an externally reachable absolute URL, then refresh the preview fetch
options.feedback: Correct. The page Hero image and share-card input are separate paths, so inspect the og:image value and reachability.

options.label: Keep cropping the page Hero image until the sharing platform discovers it automatically
options.feedback: Cropping the page image does not write Open Graph metadata or guarantee that the external platform reads it.

options.label: Only add body keywords because Open Graph is for search ranking
options.feedback: Open Graph primarily describes shared-link previews, not search ranking; body keywords cannot replace og:image.

data.agentPrompt: Add the article's Open Graph title, description, absolute image URL, and canonical URL. Do not treat the page Hero image as proof; verify the title, description, and image in an external share preview, and record evidence if platform caching keeps an old result.
